input.summary:
Glazing, doors and shutters (parts/fittings.mjs) is written as intended, but its 230 window and door writes are refused because shell-west fills every opening with air first, so the lock owns those cells.
OFF-PALETTE is already clean for this part (0 blocks), so fittings.mjs is unchanged. make.sh exits 0 and produces build.nbt, but the wall openings are bare.
Not finished: the fix belongs in shell-west.mjs, which I was not allowed to edit.
left: BLOCKED upstream, not fixed here: parts/shell-west.mjs house() fills the wall body and then each hole with air (g.fill air at line 23), and the gambrel ends get an air fill at line 77. runParts treats any earlier write, air included, as owned, so every window, door and shutter in fittings.mjs is refused (230 REFUSED). I did not remove or move those writes: that would leave every opening bare and hide the problem, and getting past the lock would mean bypassing runParts.

Verified in a scratch copy (deleted; real files untouched): if house() writes body only outside hole cells and drops the hole air fill, fittings refusals fall from 230 to 8 and its placed count rises from 237 to 459. The 8 left are the plot 3 gambrel end pairs (x51 and x61, y6..7), owned by the line-77 air fill.

Fix options for the owner: (a) in shell-west, leave opening cells unwritten (no body, no air) and remove the line-77 gambrel air fill; or (b) change runParts so a later part may fill air an earlier part left as a declared opening. Option (a) is smaller and needs no library change. After it lands, re-run ./make.sh: fittings should show no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE.
Other parts still show REFUSED in make.sh (roofs 83, porches 23, chimneys 10, rooms P3/P5/P7). Not touched here.

waste.what: Tracing which earlier part owned each refused cell: reading runParts' owned set, shell-west's house() holes, and the gambrel fill by hand, then testing the fix in a scratch copy
waste.cost: About 8 tool calls and one full build run to confirm the cause
waste.tool: parts-report.json should name the owning part and write (e.g. shell west, air, line 23) for each refusal and say whether the cell is a declared opening; refusedAt is capped at 8, which hid that all 230 share one cause

waste.what: Checking that the palette report was clean for this part by hand-reading parts-report.json
waste.tool: make.sh could print a one-line verdict per part (refused, off-palette, placed)

waste.what: Plan contradiction: plan.md says openings stay air in Parts 1-2 and Part 5 fills them, but the runParts lock makes that impossible
waste.cost: Found only by reading the library lock code; no tool flagged it
waste.tool: A plan lint or runParts option (e.g. openings: [...] on the shell) that lets a later part fill declared openings and fails the build on this contradiction
